plugins.description: A portable memory protocol for AI agents — load it as standing rules; a curation discipline + reference spec + optional cap hook.
plugins.readme_text:
**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

# Engramory

[![CI](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Python 3.9+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.9%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)

**An opinionated, zero-infrastructure memory *protocol* for small-scale, local,
file-based agent memory** — a strict curation discipline plus a validator
(`tools/engramory_doctor.py`), loaded as **standing rules** (`CLAUDE.md` /
`AGENTS.md` / your host's rules file). It is not a database, a framework, or a
relevance-loaded skill. Memory is a folder of small, human-readable markdown files
plus one always-loaded index. No database, no embeddings, no server — just
plain-text files you can open, read, edit, and diff in any editor (the live store
itself stays git-ignored).

> *Engramory* — coined from *engram* (the physical trace a memory leaves in the
> brain) + *memory*. Here: one file = one fact.

> ⚠️ **Unrelated projects share this name.** *engram + memory* is an obvious
> coinage and at least one other repository arrived at it independently. This
> project is only ever `tinqiao-oss/engramory` (npm: `dsh-engramory`); a same-named
> repo under a different owner is not a fork, a mirror, or a newer version of it.

> 🤖 **Are you an AI agent, asked to install or check this?** Start at
> **[AGENT-SETUP.md](AGENT-SETUP.md)**, not at the install steps below. It is the
> procedure for working out what your host can actually enforce, whether a store
> already exists, what you must not touch, and what to tell the user — the parts
> agents reliably get wrong when improvising.

> **Status: 0.12.1 — experimental.** The hard index cap (a `PreToolUse` hook) is
> deterministic for the matched direct-edit tools (`Edit | Write | MultiEdit`) but
> NOT a global write guard (shell tools — Bash, PowerShell, a background Monitor
> command — plus MCP file tools, external editors, and sync clients bypass it);
> the discipline loads as standing rules the model follows, so it's
> best-effort, not guaranteed on every task (see [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) §8). Assumes a
> single writer / serialized writes. Don't rely on it as a "mandatory, reliable,
> cross-agent" memory layer yet.

---

## What this is — and is NOT

Engramory is **not a new memory architecture**. The "markdown files + a small index
loaded into context + the model curates it" pattern is now the mainstream shape
for agent memory, and it ships in several places already. Engramory stands on:

- **Claude Code native auto-memory** — the same markdown-`MEMORY.md`-index +
  lazy detail-file pattern; its system prompt even uses the same
  `user | feedback | project | reference` type vocabulary (per
  [anthropics/claude-code#58840](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/58840);
  the *public docs* describe only the index + topic files). Engramory is a
  disciplined superset of this default.
- **[basic-memory](https://github.com/basicmachines-co/basic-memory)** — markdown
  source-of-truth, YAML frontmatter `type`, `[[wikilink]]` graph, local-first.
- **[obsidian-second-brain](https://github.com/eugeniughelbur/obsidian-second-brain)**,
  **[claude-memory-compiler](https://github.com/coleam00/claude-memory-compiler)**
  ("a loaded index beats vector search at personal scale"), and the broader family
  of markdown-memory skills.

What Engramory contributes is the **opinionated bundle + the discipline**, not the
primitives. Do not claim novelty on markdown, frontmatter, wikilinks, a loaded
index, one-file-per-fact notes, or curation hygiene — all are prior art.

## What's actually differentiated

1. **A role/purpose ontology, headed by `feedback` = procedural memory.** The
   semantic / episodic / **procedural** split is established prior art — the CoALA
   taxonomy, and a named procedural type in LangMem and mem0 — so Engramory does not
   claim the category. What it does is make procedural `feedback` the *spine* of a
   deliberately tiny, hand-authored, human-readable set, with required **Why:** /
   **How to apply:** lines, instead of auto-extracting it into a vector/graph store.
   The contribution is the packaging and discipline, not the ontology.

2. **The curation contract as concrete behaviour** the protocol applies (model-followed, not a hard gate): dedup-before-write,
   update-don't-duplicate, delete-when-wrong, and a negative-scope rule ("don't
   store what git/CLAUDE.md/the code already records"). Surveys consistently name
   *modify/delete/forget* as the most under-implemented memory operation — Engramory
   makes it the spine.

3. **A bounded index designed not to silently rot.** The index loads every session and
   Claude Code reads the first 200 lines / 25 KB (documented behavior), so an unbounded index silently
   drops memories off the end. Engramory warns at 150 lines / 20 KB, compacts-or-asks
   before 200 / 25 KB, and ships a hard `PreToolUse` hook backstop (it blocks only
   *growth* past the cap — shrinking/compaction edits always pass). Both the line and
   byte caps apply — whichever is hit first triggers (an index can be under the line
   count yet over on bytes when the lines run long).

   Claude Code has since followed up on this natively: v2.1.186 (released
   2026-06-22) reminds the agent to compact the index when it nears the cap, and
   v2.1.210 (released 2026-07-14) turned an over-cap write into an explicit error
   instead of a silent truncation. Both are after-the-fact alerts, though — the
   write still lands, and entries past the cap stay invisible until someone
   compacts. Engramory's hook denies the write *before* it happens, so a write
   through the matched edit tools never leaves the index over-cap in the first
   place (writes outside them — a shell, an MCP file tool — are not gated; see the
   status note above and SKILL.md §8). The native alerts validate the direction
   and make a welcome second layer — and older versions and other hosts still
   have neither.

## How it compares

| | storage | recall | human-readable | typed ontology | curation discipline | bounded index | infra |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Engramory** | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ role-based (4) | ✅ contract (model-run) | ✅ 150/200 + hook | none |
| CC auto-memory | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ same 4 types | partial (auto) | ~200-line window* | none (built-in) |
| basic-memory | md + SQLite | semantic/FTS search | ✅ | ✅ freeform type | schema + overwrite checks | ❌ (no loaded index) | SQLite + embeddings |
| obsidian-second-brain | md vault | index-first + search | ✅ | folder-typed | ✅ reconcile/lint | partial | none |
| mem0 / Zep | vector/graph DB | semantic | ❌ (DB) | typed (prefs/episodic/proc.; Zep custom) | auto-extract | n/a | DB + embeddings |
| [agentmemory](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory) | SQLite + vector index (+opt. graph) | hybrid BM25+vector (+opt. graph), RRF | ❌ (DB/engine) | ✅ 4-tier lifecycle (work./epis./sem./proc.) | auto (capture + dedup + decay) | n/a | iii engine (local) + opt. embeddings |

Engramory's lane: **minimalism + actionable role typing + curation discipline, zero
infra.** It does *not* try to out-search basic-memory, out-scale mem0, or
out-capture agentmemory — those solve a different problem (auto-capture /
auto-ingest at volume) at a different cost point. agentmemory is the closest
heavyweight foil: also local-first, but it bets on automatic capture (lifecycle
hooks) + hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vectors + optional graph) on a SQLite/`iii`
engine, where Engramory bets on hand-curation + a tiny always-loaded index and
ships no engine at all.

\* Claude Code's [memory docs](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/memory)
document this exactly: *"the first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB,
whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation."* Other hosts
vary, so the window stays configurable via the hook's env vars.

## Where it fits — and the goal

Engramory is a **portable memory *discipline*, not a

plugins.description: 复杂项目模式 preset for DeepSeek Harness (dsh): the standard tool stack plus a four-document policy, current-state-only docs, a no-unrequested-push rule, careful coding, and plain-language reporting.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-complex-project-preset

**An agent preset for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): the full standard tool stack, plus the discipline to think before it types.**

> 中文版: [README.zh.md](README.zh.md)

The whole preset lives in [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml): it inserts one `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` row into the profile and registers a preset with the id `complex-project`. The package ships **configuration only** — no host code, no browser UI — so there is very little that an upgrade can break.

---

## Why

The standard preset gets work done, but it will not hold a line on its own: diffs creep, project docs turn into changelogs, and code goes up before you said so.

This preset writes four rules into the persona prompt, so every session starts with them already in force:

| Rule | In one line |
| --- | --- |
| Four documents | A project keeps at most four docs: intro, decisions, change log, current state & next steps |
| Current state only | No AI edit history, no superseded decisions, no leftover "stage 1–5" wording |
| Commit/push red line | No `git commit`, `git push`, or PR until you explicitly say so |
| Careful coding + plain language | Restate the goal and the done-criteria first, make surgical diffs, lead reports with the conclusion |

## What's inside

The tool stack matches the standard preset — bash/pwsh chosen per platform, file read/write and search, tasks and background jobs, skills, plan mode, compaction, subagents and workflows, web fetch, the TODO tool, present. What differs is the persona prompt and the documentation rules:

- `persona` — the four-document policy, current-state-only docs, the commit/push red line, the careful-coding rules, and plain-language reporting;
- `agent-instructions` — still loads your global `AGENTS.md` (64 KB cap);
- `planning` / `compaction` / `delegation` — same groups and isolation settings as standard;
- `tool-plugin-manager` — disabled, so the agent cannot rewrite its own plugin tree.

> ⚠️ The persona block deliberately sets **no `suffix`**. DSH registers only `provider` and `model` as prompt variables; any other `{{name}}` throws during prompt assembly and the whole turn fails before a single request is sent. The working directory is injected by the runtime context already, so declaring it here is redundant as well as fatal.

## Install

```sh
# from npm (recommended — prebuilt install, no build approval)
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-complex-project-preset

# or from the repository / a local directory
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/sueqet/dsh-complex-project-preset
dsh plugin --profile web add link:<local-dir>
```

**Restart the profile** (run `dsh web` again, or restart the desktop app) — a preset is a row in the profile composition, not a runtime hot-load.

Uninstall: `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-complex-project-preset`

### Conflicts with a hand-rolled copy

If your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` already declares `- id: preset-complex-project` by hand, installing this package registers the same preset twice and DSH reports `Duplicate agent preset: complex-project`. To switch over:

1. delete that `- id: preset-complex-project ...` block from your `cordis.patch.yml`;
2. `dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-complex-project-preset`;
3. restart the profile.

Only one package should provide `complex-project` at a time.

### Version requirement

Requires **DSH ≥ 0.1.7-rc.2** (the preset registry `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry` joins the base composition there) and **Node.js ≥ 22.19.0**. Verified on DSH 0.1.7-rc.2 and on the desktop build 0.2.1-rc.2.

The Node floor is the harness's own rather than this package's: DSH compositions call `process.getBuiltinModule`, which Node ships from 22.3 onwards. This package is a manifest plus one YAML patch — no host code, no browser code, no install-time scripts — so it never loads JavaScript of its own, and the floor only mirrors where DSH can run at all.

## Verify

After a restart, open the mode picker for a new session: **复杂项目模式** (order 2, right after the standard preset) should be listed. Start a session with it and ask about the project's current state — the answer should talk in terms of the four documents rather than freeform.

From the CLI you can also inspect the composed tree:

```sh
dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -A3 preset-complex-project
```

## Develop

```sh
npm test          # checks manifest + cordis.patch.yml consistency, including !!js parsing
npm pack --dry-run
```

`tools/smoke.mjs` verifies that `dsh.bundle.patch` points at a file that exists, that `repository` points back at this repo, that every required preset field is present, that child row ids are unique, and that the persona prompt is neither truncated nor carrying a stray `suffix`. It parses the patch with the harness's own `loadOverlayPatches` when available, so `!!js` expressions behave exactly as they do at boot.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 sueqet

plugins.description: Expose the running DeepSeek Harness Web GUI's authenticated URL as an agent tool (gui_auth_url), so browser automation can open the GUI instead of failing with 401. Install: dsh plugin --profile web add github:NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-gui-auth-url

[![CI](https://github.com/NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![dsh](https://img.shields.io/badge/dsh-%3E%3D0.2.1--rc.2%20%3C0.3.0--0-6f42c1)](package.json)
[![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url?style=social)](https://github.com/NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url/stargazers)

> Third-party community plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Not an official DeepSeek product. MIT licensed.

English | [中文](README-zh.md) | [Español](README-es.md) | [Português](README-pt.md) | [हिन्दी](README-hi.md)

Expose the running DeepSeek Harness Web GUI's **authenticated URL** as an agent tool, so browser automation and scripts can open the GUI instead of hitting `401 dsh web authentication required`.

## The problem

`dsh --profile web` mints a random launch token per process and prints it once:

```text
dsh web: http://127.0.0.1:3080/?token=...
```

`GET /?token=...` verifies the token, sets a signed cookie bound to host:port, and redirects to `/`. Opening the bare address returns:

```text
401 dsh web authentication required; reopen the URL printed by dsh web.
```

The Desktop edition starts its own Host process on a random port and never prints that line, so any external browser or automation tool opening `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` always gets 401. There is no `--no-browser-auth` switch today.

## How it works

The plugin runs inside the Host process and asks the official public API `connection.authenticatedUrl(baseUrl)` — the same call `dsh web` uses to build the URL it prints — then returns the result as a tool result.

It never reads the cookie-signing secret in `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml` and never mints a cookie itself, so the URL is a genuine first-party session bound to this process.

Base URL resolution prefers `webApp.getAdvertisedUrl()` (respects `--public-url` and mounts), then `webServer.getOrigin()`, then protocol plus loopback port. Every call re-reads the live value, so random Desktop ports and restarted tokens need no cache. The token is attached only when that base is absolute `http` or `https`, has no username or password, and — unless the plugin config sets `allowPublic: true` — names a loopback host (`127.0.0.0/8`, `localhost`, or `::1`). The returned URL must be that same origin and carry exactly one `token`. An unacceptable base is refused before `authenticatedUrl` is called, and the error text never includes the URL.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` writes the bundle into the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` automatically. Restart DeepSeek Harness and the tool appears.

Local checkout instead:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url.git
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-gui-auth-url
```

The package is published on npm as `dsh-gui-auth-url`. GitHub is the source repository.

Upgrading from the old name `dsh-gui-session` (0.1.x): the package name, Cordis row id and tool name all changed, so reinstall once:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <name> remove dsh-gui-session
dsh plugin --profile <name> add github:NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url
```

## Usage

The plugin registers one tool, `gui_auth_url`, with no parameters. It returns:

```json
{
  "url": "http://127.0.0.1:3080/?token=...",
  "origin": "http://127.0.0.1:3080",
  "protocol": "http:",
  "host": "127.0.0.1",
  "port": "3080",
  "secure": false
}
```

The model sees the `url` text; the other fields are available to programmatic callers. Hand the URL to `navigate_page`, `curl`, or any HTTP client to enter the GUI.

Typical use: while debugging DeepSeek Harness itself, let the agent open the live GUI with chrome-devtools-mcp and verify layout, interaction and RPC for real instead of guessing from code.

## Security

- The returned URL contains **this process's launch token**. It is a credential equivalent to a signed-in session and only works while the Host process is alive.
- Do not write it to logs, commit it, or paste it into chats. Regenerate by calling the tool again; a restart invalidates it.
- A successful call still places the token in the session transcript and in later model requests. "Do not write it to logs" does not stop the host from storing the tool result. That is a wider audience than the one line `dsh web` prints in a terminal.
- The plugin does not read `.credentials.yaml` and does not mint cookies.
- Non-loopback URLs (`--public-url`, a LAN address, or `0.0.0.0`) are refused unless the plugin config is exactly `allowPublic: true`. That flag trusts the advertised host.
- It is unrelated to [Discussion #8678](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/8678) (reading the signing secret inside a sandbox to forge cookies): this plugin never touches that secret.

## Compatibility

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| dsh | `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0-0` |
| Node | `>=22.19.0` |
| Verified on | dsh `0.2.1-rc.2`, Windows x64, desktop and web profiles |
| Web combination | needs the `connection` service; a profile without a Web GUI reports a clear error |

Display metadata (`locale/*.json` plus the exported `./icon`) makes the Plugins page and Settings show a proper title, description and artwork instead of the raw package id. The plugin does not require a build step: it ships plain ESM JavaScript.

## Troubleshooting

**The tool does not appear after install.** Check that the profile's `package.json` lists `dsh-gui-auth-url` in `dsh.profile.bundles`. `dsh plugin add` normally writes it, but a failed install can leave only the dependency:

```json
{
  "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["@deepseek-ai/dsh-base", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app", "dsh-gui-auth-url"] } }
}
```

Restart DeepSeek Harness, then confirm with `dsh --profile <name> --dump-config` and look for the `gui-auth-url` row.

**Installation rejected because of a version mismatch.** DSH checks `engines.dsh` (or dsh peer ranges) at install time. If your host is outside the declared range, grant the exact-version exemption, reinstall, and revoke it once a compatible release exists:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> version-exemptions
dsh plugin --profile <profile> allow-version dsh-gui-auth-url@0.2.1 --dsh-version <runtime> --accept-risk
dsh plugin --profile <profile> revoke-version dsh-gui-auth-url@0.2.1
```

**`EPERM: rename ... node_modules\dsh-gui-auth-url_tmp_*` on Windows.** Stop the DSH process using that profile, delete the stale `node_modules\dsh-gui-auth-url` directory, and retry. A running process locks the directory.

**"This profile serves no Web GUI".** The plugin only returns a URL when the profile mounts `webApp` or `webServer` plus `connection`. Headless-style profiles have no GUI to open.

**"refusing to attach the launch token to a non-loopback host".** The advertised URL is not loopback. The token is not returned. To allow that host, set this entry in the profile patch. A later patch replaces the whole `config` object, so keep any other keys you need in that same object:

```yaml
- id: gui-auth-url
  config:
    allowPublic: true
```

Leave `allowPublic` unset on a Desktop loopback profile. The flag trusts whatever `webApp.getAdvertisedUrl()` returns.

## Development

```bash
node --test test/*.test.js          # unit + manifest compliance tests
node --check src/index.js && node --check src/auth-url.js
npm run check:pack                  # verifies the published tarball contents
```

```text
src/auth-url.js    pure helpers: base URL resolution + Host session call (unit-tested)
src/index.js       Cordis plugin entry: registers the gui_auth_url tool
locale/            display metadata (en, zh, es, pt, hi)
test/              node:test suites, including packaging invariants
scripts/           tarball check used by prepublishOnly and CI
```

The plugin only registers a tool; `ctx.tools.register` returns the disposer that Cordis owns, so unloading or hot-reloading the pl

plugins.description: bioRxiv preprint search, version/status and export tools for DeepSeek Harness (dsh). Zero runtime dependencies.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-biorxiv

bioRxiv preprint search, version/publication status and export tools for DeepSeek Harness (dsh). Zero runtime dependencies.

> Status: `0.1.0-alpha` — functional core, not a 1.0 release. Relevance evaluation is provisional; do not treat it as peer-reviewed evidence.

## Tools

- `biorxiv_search` — search bioRxiv preprints by topic, optional date window and field. Default `minScore=3` filters low-confidence text matches; set `minScore=0` for higher recall.
- `biorxiv_paper` — DOI lookup: latest version, publication DOI/journal, retraction flag when available.
- `biorxiv_latest` — latest preprints by date window and optional category.
- `biorxiv_export` — export search results or one DOI as JSON, Markdown, CSV or BibTeX.
- `biorxiv_digest` — structured markdown digest (extractive by default; optional opt-in Chinese summaries; no automatic delivery).

All tools return a stable envelope:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {},
  "error": { "code": "", "message": "", "retryable": false, "hint": "" },
  "meta": { "requestId": "...", "elapsedMs": 12, "cached": false, "source": ["europepmc"], "warnings": [] }
}
```

On failure `ok` is `false`, `data` is `{}`, and `error.code` is one of `E-001`–`E-010`.

## Install (one command)

```bash
dsh plugin --profile headless add github:TYEclipse/dsh-biorxiv#v0.1.0-alpha.20
```

Replace `headless` with the target profile. `dsh plugin add` is a pnpm forwarder: a `--profile` is required, and `pnpm` must be on `PATH`.

Build from source instead:

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm pack
dsh plugin --profile headless add "file:$PWD/$(ls -t dsh-biorxiv-*.tgz | head -1)"
```

Verify:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile headless list
dsh --profile headless "Use biorxiv_search to search for 'protein language model' and report the first title and DOI."
```

`dsh plugin add` is a pnpm forwarder: a `--profile` is required, and `pnpm` must be on `PATH`.

## CLI

```bash
dsh-biorxiv search "protein language model" --limit 5
dsh-biorxiv paper 10.64898/2026.07.21.739963
dsh-biorxiv latest --days 2 --limit 10
dsh-biorxiv export "hippocampal ripple" --format markdown --out refs.md
dsh-biorxiv digest "protein language model" --limit 5
```

Each command prints one JSON envelope and exits `0` on success, `1` on a tool error, `2` on a usage error.

## MCP

Run the stdio server:

```bash
dsh-biorxiv-mcp
```

MCP client config example:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "biorxiv": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "--package", "dsh-biorxiv", "dsh-biorxiv-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

An npm package is not published yet. The `npx` form above works after publication; for a GitHub install, point the client at `node ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/dsh-biorxiv/dist/apps/mcp/main.js`.

The server exposes `biorxiv_search`, `biorxiv_paper`, `biorxiv_latest`, `biorxiv_export` and `biorxiv_digest` with the same JSON envelope.

## Configuration

Defaults live in the plugin schema; no config is required.

```json
{
  "cachePath": "~/.cache/dsh-biorxiv/cache.db",
  "cacheMode": "auto",
  "timeoutMs": 10000,
  "retries": 2,
  "maxBytes": 2000000,
  "userAgent": "dsh-biorxiv/0.1 (DeepSeek Harness plugin)",
  "summaryEnabled": false,
  "summaryModel": "deepseek-chat",
  "summaryBaseUrl": "https://api.deepseek.com",
  "summaryApiKeyEnv": "DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"
}
```

- `summaryEnabled`: default `false`. When true, `digest --summary` sends only public title/abstract to the configured model and labels output as machine-generated.
- The API key is read from the named environment variable; it is never written to config, cache or logs.
- CLI: `dsh-biorxiv digest "topic" --summary` opts in; it also enables the provider for that process.
- MCP: set `DSH_BIORXIV_SUMMARY=1` in the server environment, then call `biorxiv_digest` with `summary: true`.

- `cacheMode`: `auto` (SQLite when available, JSON fallback), `sqlite`, or `json`.
- Cache keys are SHA-256 hashes; query text is not written into the cache key.
- Delete the cache file to reset; it is disposable.

## Data sources and boundaries

- Search: Europe PMC REST (`SRC:PPR` + `PUBLISHER:"bioRxiv"`).
- Latest/version details: bioRxiv public API.
- Journal/retraction enrichment: Crossref and OpenAlex; failures are non-blocking.
- No full-text PDF download, no scraping behind 403/paywalls, no writes to source sites.
- Do not use for clinical, medical or investment decisions. Preprints are not peer-reviewed.

## Development

```bash
pnpm test
pnpm coverage
```

The coverage ratchet is enforced by `scripts/coverage-ratchet.mjs`; line coverage must not fall below `.coverage-baseline.json`.

## License

MIT. See `LICENSE`. Privacy and data flow: see `PRIVACY.md`.

plugins.description: Deterministic financial-data and valuation plugin for DeepSeek Harness: six ratio groups, forecast ratios, DCF slots, comparable PS/PE, IRR — one unified schema.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-valuation-service

A deterministic financial-data and valuation plugin for **DeepSeek Harness**. It reads a workpaper layout of `01.json` / `02.json` / `04.json`, computes six ratio groups, forecast ratios, DCF input slots, comparable PS / PE and IRR, and writes one unified schema per project set.

It registers one agent tool, **`valuation_service`**. No AI inference, no invented numbers: anything missing is left blank and marked `missing` for a human or a downstream research step to fill.

## What it computes

| Block | Content |
|---|---|
| `ratios.historical` | profitability, solvency, efficiency, cash flow, valuation, growth |
| `ratios.forecast` | forecast-period profitability / growth / expense; BS- and CF-dependent ratios marked missing |
| `dcf` | full input slots (WACC, g, tax, EBIT, D&A, capex, ΔWC, net debt), outputs, missing list, hand-off anchors |
| `comparable` | PS and PE in parallel: trimmed mean, all-sample mean, 1-year mean, pre-money multiple, premium |
| `irr` | target / conservative / optimistic, closed-vs-open judgement, deviation |
| `assumption_diff` | material assumptions vs assumptions computed from actuals, field by field |
| `pending` / `gate` | unresolved conflicts and C2–C7 gate status when the workpapers carry them |

## Input layout

```text
<base>/
├── 项目A/
│   └── json/
│       ├── 01.json   # financial.raw (BS/IS/CF) + financial.ratios
│       ├── 02.json   # assumptions.forecast + assumptions.comparables + assumptions.valuation
│       └── 04.json   # validation.irr_recompute
└── 项目B/
    └── json/...
```

`--base` defaults to `$DSH_VALUATION_BASE` or `./数据底表`. Projects are discovered dynamically: every directory with all three JSON files is included. No project list is hard-coded.

`01.json` may use either `raw = {bs, is, cf}` or report-title sections (e.g. `"一、资产负债表 · 资产"`); both are normalized.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin add https://github.com/zirscard/dsh-valuation-service
```

Or from a local directory:

```bash
dsh plugin add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-valuation-service
```

Restart DSH; a new session gets the `valuation_service` tool.

## Tool usage

```json
{
  "base": "/path/to/数据底表",
  "projects": "项目A,项目B",
  "write": true
}
```

- `base` (string, optional): workpaper root; relative paths resolve against the session working directory.
- `projects` (string or array, optional): restrict to these project directory names.
- `write` (boolean, optional, default `false`): write `<base>/valuations-service.json`.
- `out` (string, optional): override the output path.

The tool returns a per-project summary (DCF status and missing list, PS/PE status, IRR closed flag, assumption-diff count, gate) plus the output path.

## CLI usage

The Python entry point is usable without DSH (standard library only):

```bash
python3 core/valuation_service.py --base /path/to/数据底表 --dry-run
python3 core/valuation_service.py --base /path/to/数据底表 --projects 项目A
python3 core/valuation_service.py --base /path/to/数据底表 --write
python3 core/valuation_service.py --base /path/to/数据底表 --write --json
```

`--json` prints one machine-readable summary object; `--write` writes the aggregate file; without `--write` it is a dry run.

## Unified schema

```json
{
  "schema": "m1.valuation-service/v2",
  "project_id": "...",
  "project_name": "...",
  "currency": "CNY",
  "method": "...",
  "financial_inputs": {"period": "...", "is": {}, "bs": {}, "cf": {}},
  "ratios": {"historical": {}, "forecast": {}},
  "dcf": {"status": "computed|partial|unavailable", "inputs": {}, "outputs": {}, "missing": [], "m3_handoff": {}},
  "comparable": {"ps": {}, "pe": {}},
  "irr": {"target": null, "conservative": null, "optimistic": null, "closed": false, "judge": "", "dev": null},
  "assumption_diff": [],
  "pending": [],
  "gate": {}
}
```

The aggregate file wraps records as `{"schema": "m1.valuation-service/aggregate/v2", "generated_at": "...", "base": "...", "projects": [...], "errors": [...]}`.

## Formulas

- Ratios: gross / operating / net margin, ROE, ROA; current / quick / cash ratio, debt-to-equity, debt-to-assets, interest coverage; asset / inventory / receivables turnover and days; OCF ratios; PS / PE / EV / EV-EBITDA; revenue and net-income growth.
- DCF: `FCFF = EBIT × (1 − t) + D&A − capex − ΔWC`; `TV = FCFF_last × (1 + g) / (WACC − g)`; `EV = Σ PV(FCFF) + PV(TV)`; `equity = EV − net debt`.
- Comparable: trimmed mean (10% each side when n ≥ 5), all-sample mean, 1-year mean, pre-money multiple, premium.
- IRR: `(exit value / invested capital) ^ (1 / years) − 1`.
- Assumption diff: material assumption vs module-computed actual, per field.

Ratio formulas are adapted from [anthropics/claude-cookbooks · analyzing-financial-statements/calculate_ratios.py](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-cookbooks/blob/main/skills/custom_skills/analyzing-financial-statements/calculate_ratios.py) (MIT), mapped onto Chinese three-statement labels.

## Adaptation layer

Data variants are handled in one place instead of per project:

| Variant | Function | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| raw layout (`{bs,is,cf}` vs report-title sections) | `_normalize_raw` | normalize by 资产负债表 / 利润表 / 现金流量表 keywords |
| units (thousand / ten-thousand / million CNY) | `_unit_for` | field-name suffix first, then `forecast.unit` |
| field-name variants | `_find_param` | keyword match + exclusion words |
| total vs line item (`资产总计` vs `流动资产合计`) | `_find_val` | totals require an exact match, no substring fallback |
| self-comparison in the comp set | `_included` | drop rows whose `treatment` says 自比 / 剔除 |
| no market PE multiple | `comparable.pe.status=assumption` | use the assumption range explicitly, never present it as a market multiple |

If a new variant is structural (layout / unit / naming), add it to the adapter. If it is a measurement convention, add it to the skill formulas. If data is missing, leave it blank and mark `missing`.

## DCF hand-off

Missing DCF inputs stay blank; `dcf.m3_handoff.anchors` lists what each one needs:

| Missing input | Anchor to fill |
|---|---|
| WACC | risk-free rate / beta / equity risk premium / capital structure |
| g | long-run GDP growth / industry terminal growth |
| capex | capex plan / construction in progress / capacity expansion |
| D&A | depreciation and amortization policy |
| ΔWC | receivables / inventory / payables turnover forecast |
| tax rate | effective tax rate |
| net debt | interest-bearing debt − cash |

## Test

```bash
python3 test/run_tests.py
```

The test builds a synthetic three-project workpaper set in a temporary directory (no client data), runs the service, and checks ratio values, DCF missing slots, comparable status, IRR and the written aggregate file.

## Boundaries

- No AI inference, no model calls, no network requests.
- No client data or project names are shipped in this repository.
- Missing inputs are marked, not fabricated.
- It does not replace a valuation model: it standardizes inputs and keeps the slots.

## License

MIT. Ratio formulas adapted from anthropics/claude-cookbooks (MIT); see [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](./THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: turn sidebar entries into a compact icon row, with adjustable icon size and per-entry visibility.
plugins.readme_text:
# 侧栏图标并列（sidebar-icon-row）

DeepSeek Harness 插件的侧栏入口默认都是 42px 整行，所以「插件广场 / 远程控制 / 面板入口」会一条一行。
本插件把它们压成 36×36 的图标方块并排显示，并提供设置页。

- 面板入口（`sidebar.panellist`）与底部入口（`sidebar.footer.action`）统一处理；
- 「今日 / 余额」卡片仍独占一整行（沿用 cost-meter 自己的 `.cm-footer-stack`）；
- 每个入口只显示图标，常驻文字隐藏，悬停时在图标上方显示名称（纯 CSS `::after` + `aria-label`）；
- 侧栏收起成 56px 轨道时保持原样（图标竖排）；
- 底部新增一个「设置」齿轮入口，一键打开 DSH 设置页；
- 设置页里可调图标大小（16 / 18 / 20 / 24）、逐个开关入口、并调整图标先后顺序。

## 实现方式

- 只注入一个 `<style>` 节点，不修改任何宿主或其他插件的组件；
- 选择器用 `[data-slot="sidebar.footer.action"] > *` 与 `[class*="panelList"]` / `[class*="panelRow"]` 锚定，
  不使用 `_2H3hWW_` 这类带构建哈希的类名；
- 侧栏入口按渲染出来的名字（`aria-label` 优先）打上 `data-sir-key`，隐藏与排序都作用在这个属性上，
  关闭的入口直接 `display: none !important`（内联），所以不依赖选择器优先级；
- 排序通过给每个入口写 `order` 实现，不移动 DOM；
- 设置存在浏览器 `localStorage`（键 `dsh.sidebar-icon-row.v1`），按浏览器各自保存。

## 设置页

`插件 → 已安装插件 → 侧栏图标并列`。设置区注册在 `plugins.bundle.config`（key 为包名），
在插件页描述下方、插件行上方渲染。

## 安装 / 卸载

```powershell
# 安装（当前 profile；源码就放在 profile 的 local-plugins 下，不依赖工作区）
dsh plugin install "E:\DeepseekHarness-data\data\profiles\desktop\local-plugins\sidebar-icon-row"
# 卸载
dsh plugin remove dsh-sidebar-icon-row
```

安装后刷新页面；新增 bundle 首次加载可能需要重启一次 `dsh web`。

## 回滚

在插件管理里关掉「侧栏图标并列」，或卸载本包：样式随 `<style>` 清理消失，
额外的「设置」图标随 `sidebar.footer.action` 的注册一并移除。

plugins.description: A portable memory protocol for AI agents — load it as standing rules; a curation discipline + reference spec + optional cap hook.
plugins.readme_text:
**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

# Engramory

[![CI](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Python 3.9+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.9%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)

**An opinionated, zero-infrastructure memory *protocol* for small-scale, local,
file-based agent memory** — a strict curation discipline plus a validator
(`tools/engramory_doctor.py`), loaded as **standing rules** (`CLAUDE.md` /
`AGENTS.md` / your host's rules file). It is not a database, a framework, or a
relevance-loaded skill. Memory is a folder of small, human-readable markdown files
plus one always-loaded index. No database, no embeddings, no server — just
plain-text files you can open, read, edit, and diff in any editor (the live store
itself stays git-ignored).

> *Engramory* — coined from *engram* (the physical trace a memory leaves in the
> brain) + *memory*. Here: one file = one fact.

> ⚠️ **Unrelated projects share this name.** *engram + memory* is an obvious
> coinage and at least one other repository arrived at it independently. This
> project is only ever `tinqiao-oss/engramory` (npm: `dsh-engramory`); a same-named
> repo under a different owner is not a fork, a mirror, or a newer version of it.

> 🤖 **Are you an AI agent, asked to install or check this?** Start at
> **[AGENT-SETUP.md](AGENT-SETUP.md)**, not at the install steps below. It is the
> procedure for working out what your host can actually enforce, whether a store
> already exists, what you must not touch, and what to tell the user — the parts
> agents reliably get wrong when improvising.

> **Status: 0.12.1 — experimental.** The hard index cap (a `PreToolUse` hook) is
> deterministic for the matched direct-edit tools (`Edit | Write | MultiEdit`) but
> NOT a global write guard (shell tools — Bash, PowerShell, a background Monitor
> command — plus MCP file tools, external editors, and sync clients bypass it);
> the discipline loads as standing rules the model follows, so it's
> best-effort, not guaranteed on every task (see [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) §8). Assumes a
> single writer / serialized writes. Don't rely on it as a "mandatory, reliable,
> cross-agent" memory layer yet.

---

## What this is — and is NOT

Engramory is **not a new memory architecture**. The "markdown files + a small index
loaded into context + the model curates it" pattern is now the mainstream shape
for agent memory, and it ships in several places already. Engramory stands on:

- **Claude Code native auto-memory** — the same markdown-`MEMORY.md`-index +
  lazy detail-file pattern; its system prompt even uses the same
  `user | feedback | project | reference` type vocabulary (per
  [anthropics/claude-code#58840](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/58840);
  the *public docs* describe only the index + topic files). Engramory is a
  disciplined superset of this default.
- **[basic-memory](https://github.com/basicmachines-co/basic-memory)** — markdown
  source-of-truth, YAML frontmatter `type`, `[[wikilink]]` graph, local-first.
- **[obsidian-second-brain](https://github.com/eugeniughelbur/obsidian-second-brain)**,
  **[claude-memory-compiler](https://github.com/coleam00/claude-memory-compiler)**
  ("a loaded index beats vector search at personal scale"), and the broader family
  of markdown-memory skills.

What Engramory contributes is the **opinionated bundle + the discipline**, not the
primitives. Do not claim novelty on markdown, frontmatter, wikilinks, a loaded
index, one-file-per-fact notes, or curation hygiene — all are prior art.

## What's actually differentiated

1. **A role/purpose ontology, headed by `feedback` = procedural memory.** The
   semantic / episodic / **procedural** split is established prior art — the CoALA
   taxonomy, and a named procedural type in LangMem and mem0 — so Engramory does not
   claim the category. What it does is make procedural `feedback` the *spine* of a
   deliberately tiny, hand-authored, human-readable set, with required **Why:** /
   **How to apply:** lines, instead of auto-extracting it into a vector/graph store.
   The contribution is the packaging and discipline, not the ontology.

2. **The curation contract as concrete behaviour** the protocol applies (model-followed, not a hard gate): dedup-before-write,
   update-don't-duplicate, delete-when-wrong, and a negative-scope rule ("don't
   store what git/CLAUDE.md/the code already records"). Surveys consistently name
   *modify/delete/forget* as the most under-implemented memory operation — Engramory
   makes it the spine.

3. **A bounded index designed not to silently rot.** The index loads every session and
   Claude Code reads the first 200 lines / 25 KB (documented behavior), so an unbounded index silently
   drops memories off the end. Engramory warns at 150 lines / 20 KB, compacts-or-asks
   before 200 / 25 KB, and ships a hard `PreToolUse` hook backstop (it blocks only
   *growth* past the cap — shrinking/compaction edits always pass). Both the line and
   byte caps apply — whichever is hit first triggers (an index can be under the line
   count yet over on bytes when the lines run long).

   Claude Code has since followed up on this natively: v2.1.186 (released
   2026-06-22) reminds the agent to compact the index when it nears the cap, and
   v2.1.210 (released 2026-07-14) turned an over-cap write into an explicit error
   instead of a silent truncation. Both are after-the-fact alerts, though — the
   write still lands, and entries past the cap stay invisible until someone
   compacts. Engramory's hook denies the write *before* it happens, so a write
   through the matched edit tools never leaves the index over-cap in the first
   place (writes outside them — a shell, an MCP file tool — are not gated; see the
   status note above and SKILL.md §8). The native alerts validate the direction
   and make a welcome second layer — and older versions and other hosts still
   have neither.

## How it compares

| | storage | recall | human-readable | typed ontology | curation discipline | bounded index | infra |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Engramory** | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ role-based (4) | ✅ contract (model-run) | ✅ 150/200 + hook | none |
| CC auto-memory | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ same 4 types | partial (auto) | ~200-line window* | none (built-in) |
| basic-memory | md + SQLite | semantic/FTS search | ✅ | ✅ freeform type | schema + overwrite checks | ❌ (no loaded index) | SQLite + embeddings |
| obsidian-second-brain | md vault | index-first + search | ✅ | folder-typed | ✅ reconcile/lint | partial | none |
| mem0 / Zep | vector/graph DB | semantic | ❌ (DB) | typed (prefs/episodic/proc.; Zep custom) | auto-extract | n/a | DB + embeddings |
| [agentmemory](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory) | SQLite + vector index (+opt. graph) | hybrid BM25+vector (+opt. graph), RRF | ❌ (DB/engine) | ✅ 4-tier lifecycle (work./epis./sem./proc.) | auto (capture + dedup + decay) | n/a | iii engine (local) + opt. embeddings |

Engramory's lane: **minimalism + actionable role typing + curation discipline, zero
infra.** It does *not* try to out-search basic-memory, out-scale mem0, or
out-capture agentmemory — those solve a different problem (auto-capture /
auto-ingest at volume) at a different cost point. agentmemory is the closest
heavyweight foil: also local-first, but it bets on automatic capture (lifecycle
hooks) + hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vectors + optional graph) on a SQLite/`iii`
engine, where Engramory bets on hand-curation + a tiny always-loaded index and
ships no engine at all.

document this exactly: *"the first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB,

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin for the DSH Mobile Android app: QR pairing, DSH on your phone, answer approvals from notifications.
plugins.readme_text:
# DSH Mobile — host plugin for DeepSeek Harness

English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) | [日本語](README.ja.md)

`@kinocode/dsh-mobile` is a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin for the DSH Mobile Android app. It lets you:

- Pair your phone by scanning a QR code in the DSH sidebar.
- Use the regular DSH web UI on your phone through an HTTPS gateway running on your computer.
- Answer approval requests and agent questions from notifications in the live desktop session (the first answer from any device wins).
- Receive a notification when a watched session finishes its turn.

The Android app is distributed separately and is not part of this repository. This is an unofficial project, not affiliated with DeepSeek.

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0`. The range is pinned because the plugin relies on internal DSH Gateway APIs that are not yet stable.
- The DSH web server (`webserver` service), included with DSH Desktop.
- Node.js 22.4 or later (the runtime bundled with DSH Desktop works).
- Phone and computer on the same network, or both on [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com/).
- For notifications: a relay server (see [Notifications and the relay](#notifications-and-the-relay)).

## Install

Add `@kinocode/dsh-mobile` on the DSH Plugins page, or run:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add @kinocode/dsh-mobile
```

Restart DSH. The log should show `[mobile-bridge] gateway listening {"origins":[...]}`.

## Pair a phone

1. Click **スマホを接続** ("Connect phone") at the bottom of the DSH sidebar.
2. In the app, tap **QR を読み取る** ("Scan QR") and scan the code. If you do not have a camera, use **リンクをコピー** ("Copy link") and paste the link into the app.
3. The code is single-use and expires after 5 minutes. Click **新しい QR** ("New QR") to generate another.

The panel also lists paired phones and lets you remove them. Removing a phone revokes its access immediately. The panel is currently available only in Japanese.

On the phone, the DSH sidebar is hidden so the conversation gets the full width. The round button at the top left opens it over the conversation; picking a session or tapping outside closes it. Desktop-only buttons are hidden.

When you add a workspace on the phone, the computer's folders are listed on the phone instead of opening a folder dialog on the computer. Browse to a folder or type its path, then tap **このフォルダを使う** ("Use this folder").

The right sidebar (files, preview, changes review, browser, terminal) opens full screen on the phone. Buttons that open an app or Finder on the computer are hidden on the phone; the file preview offers **スマホに保存** ("Save to phone") instead, which saves to the phone's Downloads. If the page stays blank after DSH restarts, it reloads by itself.

The round buttons at the top left (sidebar) and top right (right sidebar) can be moved anywhere: long-press one, then drag it.

In DSH's built-in browser (the right sidebar's Browser), words that are not an address are searched: Google on the desktop, Bing on the phone. The phone can only show pages that allow being framed (Google and others refuse), so ↗ (Open in system browser) opens the page in Chrome.

## Configuration

All fields are optional. Add them to your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. A profile patch replaces the plugin's entire configuration, so include every field you want to keep.

```yaml
- id: mobile-bridge
  config:
    relayUrl: https://relay.example.com
    relayEnrollToken: '...'
```

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `relayUrl` | `''` (off) | Relay used for notifications and answering from them. |
| `relayEnrollToken` | `''` | Token for a relay that only accepts known computers. |
| `gatewayEnabled` | `true` | Run the HTTPS gateway for phones. |
| `gatewayPort` | `3543` | Gateway port (1024–65535). |
| `gatewayHosts` | detected | IPv4 addresses to listen on. Only private addresses are accepted (see below). |
| `hostLabel` | computer name | Name shown on the phone. |
| `previewMaxChars` | `400` | Longest command preview shown in the app (50–4000). |
| `stateDir` | `$DSH_HOME/mobile-bridge` | Absolute path for host identity, paired devices, and certificates. `$DSH_HOME` defaults to `~/.dsh`. |

The configuration ID `mobile-bridge` and log name `dsh-mobile-bridge` are kept for compatibility with earlier versions.

## How it works

- **Gateway.** The HTTPS server listens only on private IPv4 addresses: `10/8`, `172.16/12`, `192.168/16`, and Tailscale's `100.64/10`. Certificates come from a CA created by the plugin. The QR code contains the CA fingerprint, so the app trusts only that CA for this computer.
- **Pairing.** The app generates an ECDSA P-256 key in the Android Keystore and registers the public key using the one-time code.
- **Control requests.** Requests for the pending list, answers, and settings are signed with the device key. The plugin verifies the signature, a timestamp (±5 minutes), and a nonce to prevent replay attacks.
- **DSH screen.** After pairing, the app receives a 12-hour gateway session signed with a secret that never leaves the computer. Removing the device revokes it immediately. The gateway logs in to the local DSH web server directly; the phone never receives DSH's own login.
- **Live session.** The plugin connects to the DSH Gateway event stream in-process as an owner client, like an additional GUI window. Because it registers no approval listener, it cannot take requests away from the desktop or bypass it. The Gateway accepts the first answer submitted and closes the prompt everywhere else.
- **Desktop panel.** The sidebar panel uses owner-only DSH API routes (`/api/dsh-mobile-bridge/*`).

## Notifications and the relay

A phone on mobile data cannot reach the gateway directly, so notifications go through a relay. The plugin maintains an outbound WebSocket to it. The relay delivers push notifications through Firebase Cloud Messaging and forwards the phone's signed requests to your computer. It cannot create those signatures, and it never handles the DSH screen or DSH's login.

No public relay is provided. Without one, all features except notifications work as long as the phone can reach the computer directly.

What the relay can read:

- **Push messages.** By default: the session title, the tool name or question heading, up to three answer options, status, and internal IDs. If you turn on **ロック画面にコマンド全文を表示** ("Show full command on the lock screen") in the app, the relay also sees the command preview or full question (up to 400 characters) and the first 200 characters of the agent's last reply when a turn ends.
- **Requests sent through the relay.** Traffic is encrypted between each endpoint and the relay, but not end-to-end. When the phone routes requests through the relay, the relay can read the pending list (full command preview, reason, questions), the session list (titles and working directories), and your answers, including free-text replies.

Only use a relay you run yourself or trust.

On the lock screen, Android displays a short public summary unless the phone is set to show sensitive content. When DSH quits normally, the plugin tries to withdraw open notifications (waiting up to 3 seconds). If DSH crashes, the app removes stale notifications the next time it loads the pending list.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| The phone cannot connect | Are both devices on the same network or on Tailscale? Is a firewall blocking port 3543? If the computer's IP address changed, generate a new QR code. |
| "The certificate does not match the QR code" | The code is from another computer, or the gateway CA was recreated. Generate a new QR code. |
| No notifications | Are notifications enabled on the phone? Is `relayUrl` set, and does the DSH log show `relay connected`? Does the session's permission preset ask for approval? ("Full access" never does.) |
| The DSH screen is blank after a DSH restart | Close and reopen the app once DSH has finished starting. |

## Security

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) to report a vulnerability.

## Development

```bash
npm test
```

The tests use Node's built-in test runner and require no network access or external dependencies.

## License

[MIT](LICEN

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness gate - per-turn persistent-operation counter: remind, instruct the model to stop, then ask for confirmation. Steps aside under sandbox/read-only modes; follows a live permission switch without restart. Verified on real hardware (full -> workspace-write -> read-only -> full). Crafted on an estimated 0.27 USD of model spend.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-confirm-gate

**A bounded-run framework that keeps an AI agent accountable on hosts where you had to grant full permissions.**

English | [中文](README.zh-CN.md) · **v0.1.2**

> **What** — Per-turn counter for persistent operations. Gives the model a brake, not a wall.
> **Verified** — Live hot-switch on Windows (full → workspace-write → read-only → full), no restart. The model stopped itself at 11/15.
> **Cost** — ~$0.27 model spend. Zero external deps, ready-to-install archive in [`dist/`](dist/).
>
> **It steps aside under sandbox / read-only modes** — complementary to DSH's own sandbox, not a replacement.

A runtime plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It keeps a **per-turn counter of persistent operations**, injects a stop instruction once the free budget is spent, and asks the user for confirmation at a hard limit.

> **Compatibility** — built and verified against DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`; the peer range is `>=0.2.0-rc.2`, so it also loads on `0.2.1-rc.2` and later RC builds. If a future DSH release changes the tool-dispatch hooks this plugin binds to, it will fail loudly rather than silently — see [§7](#7-verifying-the-installation).

> **This is not a security boundary. It is a cost boundary and a course-correction mechanism.**
> It assumes the agent is running **without a sandbox holding the boundary**, and its purpose is to give the model **the ability to brake on its own** before it burns tokens or rewrites files. Real sandbox isolation is provided by DSH's own sandbox — complementary to this plugin, not a replacement.

*Cost figure is an author's estimate — see [`dist/COSTS.md`](dist/COSTS.md). The rest of that day went to environment diagnosis and research, not to this plugin.*

### Scope: it stays silent under a sandbox

The plugin decides, **on every tool call**, whether it should be counting. The mode comes from two sources, in priority order:

1. `ctx.sessionProjections.stateOf(session, 'permissions').sandbox` — the session's **current** knob value. This is what changes when you hot-switch modes mid-conversation.
2. `ctx.shell.sandboxMode` — the executor's **default** mode. Its own documentation calls it "the sandbox mode this executor applies by default"; it does **not** follow a hot switch, so it is only a fallback.

That distinction matters: judged from the default alone, switching into a sandbox and back would leave the plugin reading the value it saw at startup, forever.

Both reads go through `ctx.get(name)`, never `ctx.shell` directly. cordis resolves dependencies lazily, so touching an undeclared service property throws an inject-gate error — and an exception on that path once made the plugin silently do nothing at all. Soft probing cannot throw.

| Sandbox mode | Plugin counts? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `read-only` | ❌ No | The sandbox already holds every boundary |
| `workspace-write` | ❌ No | Same |
| `danger-full-access` | ✅ Yes | Nothing is holding the boundary |
| `custom` | ✅ Yes | A custom mix still leaves the boundary unheld |
| `undefined` / no shell service | ✅ Yes | This executor does not confine |
| **Unreadable (both sources threw)** | ✅ Yes | **Fail open: a silent no-op is worse than an extra reminder** |

That last row is deliberate. This plugin is an accounting tool, not a security boundary, so the two failure modes are not symmetric:

- counting when it shouldn't → a spurious reminder, immediately visible and fixable
- staying silent when it shouldn't → **the plugin appears installed but does nothing**, and nothing in the logs looks wrong

The second is far worse, so any mode it cannot read counts as "not sandboxed".

Put plainly: **under a sandbox this plugin would be redundant — and worse, it would interrupt legitimate operations a second time.** So it steps aside wherever something else is already keeping score.

Hooks are always registered; the decision is per call. That is what makes hot-switching work: move the session into a sandbox and the gate goes quiet on the very next call; move it back and counting resumes. No restart needed.

> ### ✅ Status: verified, including live hot-switching
>
> Exercised by hand on Windows, DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`. The session's permission mode
> was **switched live, without restarting DSH**, walking the sequence
> full → workspace-write → read-only → full:
>
> | Mode | Write a file | `pwsh` | Gate counted? |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | `danger-full-access` | ✅ succeeds | ✅ runs | ✅ **1/10 → 2/10 → 3/10** |
> | `workspace-write` | ✅ succeeds | ❌ fails with `0xC0000142` | ❌ silent (2 ops) |
> | `read-only` | ❌ sandbox denies | ✅ runs | ❌ silent (2 ops) |
> | `danger-full-access` again | ✅ succeeds | ✅ runs | ✅ **1/10, counting resumed** |
>
> Two things matter here. The silent rows show the division of labour working —
> the sandbox confined or rejected the operation and the gate stayed out of the
> way. The last row shows the gate coming back **in the same process**, which is
> the whole point of deciding per call instead of at load.
>
> Honest caveat: in this deployment `ctx.get('shell')` returned `undefined`, so
> the "not sandboxed" verdict came from the *unreadable, therefore fail open*
> branch rather than from a successfully read mode. The behaviour is correct;
> the path is the fallback one. A deployment that exposes `shell` would take the
> primary path instead.

### Who this is for

| Situation | Fits? |
|---|---|
| You granted full permissions and fear unbounded trial-and-error burning tokens | ✅ That is exactly the case |
| You want the agent to ask after N write operations | ✅ |
| You want `read` / `grep` / web lookups **never interrupted** | ✅ Non-persistent operations are never counted |
| You want to use it as a sandbox against a malicious model | ❌ Use DSH's built-in sandbox |
| You use a different agent framework | ❌ This is a DSH plugin |

### Trade-offs & known limitations

Listed first, because they are the interesting part.

1. **The first N operations have no gate at all.** In the default `freeLimit: 10` configuration, operations 1–10 are allowed with only a reminder. That window is deliberate — it gives the model room to correct itself before being asked to stop. Set `freeLimit: 0` when you want zero tolerance; the plugin then ask-confirms before the very first persistent operation.
2. **`confirm` defends against accidents, not injection.** The threat model is a *trusted user with a fallible model*, where the failure to prevent is unbounded trial-and-error. Prompt injection is a different layer — that is what DSH's approval channel and sandbox are for. Do not deploy this as the only thing between an untrusted input and your filesystem.
3. **The release rule is deliberately coarse.** Any message containing the trigger word releases the entire turn, including a message that merely discusses the word. This is on purpose: ambiguity is resolved by what the user typed, not by the plugin guessing intent.
4. **Command judgement is a name comparison, not a parser.** `Get-ChildItem $p.GetFiles()` is counted as persistent, because the plugin does not evaluate the pipeline. The error direction is chosen: over-count, never under-count.
5. **A tool call is one count**, regardless of how many files it touches.

### Why not X

| Alternative | Why not |
|---|---|
| **Hard-block instead of counting** | Tried first in an OpenClaw build. A wall turns every write into an interruption the user did not ask for. With a counter and an explicit stop instruction, the model does the arithmetic itself — it stopped at 11/15 on its own. The brake works better than the wall. |
| **Plugin-only, no DSH host hooks** | The per-turn count has to come from the **tool-dispatch layer**. A wrapper around the model API cannot see individual tool calls, so it cannot count them. The count lives where the calls live. |
| **Fold it into the sandbox** | Different question, different layer. A sandbox answers "is this allowed?". This answers "how much has happened?". Sitting inside the sandbox would tie a budget to a permission model that changes underneath it. |

---

## 1. Design rationale

Granting full permissions is unavoidable — a sandbox makes tools l

plugins.readme_text:
# @raullenchai/dsh-provider

A native [Rapid-MLX](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX) provider for
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) — so `dsh`
gets its model facts from the server instead of from whatever you typed into
`settings.yaml`.

[![CI](https://github.com/raullenchai/rapid-mlx-dsh-provider/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/raullenchai/rapid-mlx-dsh-provider/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

> **Status: published to npm** as
> [`@raullenchai/dsh-provider`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@raullenchai/dsh-provider).
> The end-to-end `dsh` run in [Verified](#verified) was on an M3 Ultra against
> `dsh 0.1.0-rc.7`; `dsh 0.1.0-rc.8` is API-compatible — the `LlmAdapter`
> contract is byte-identical and the only changes are additive — and the
> adapter is re-verified against rc.8 at the protocol and unit-test level.
> DSH is still a developer preview that moves fast, so treat this as tracking
> a moving target, not a frozen compatibility promise.

## What it does for you

DSH can already talk to a local Rapid-MLX server through its generic
`openai-completions` provider. That route works — but it knows nothing about
your model beyond what you hand-wrote:

```yaml
# what the generic route makes you maintain, by hand, per model
llm-pi-ai:
  providers:
    rapid-mlx:
      baseURL: http://localhost:8000/v1
      defaultContextWindow: 262144      # you looked this up. is it still right?
      models:
        - id: qwen3.6-35b-8bit
          contextWindow: 262144
          reasoningEfforts: {off: none, low: low, medium: medium, high: high}
```

Rapid-MLX's `/v1/models` already publishes all of that and more. This adapter
reads it, so:

**1. Nothing to hand-write, and nothing to re-write when you switch models.**
Swap what `rapid-mlx serve` is running and `dsh` follows. No re-running setup,
no stale numbers.

**2. The reasoning control tells the truth.** Rapid-MLX reports whether a model
actually has a reasoning parser. A model that can't reason no longer shows an
off/low/medium/high selector that does nothing.

**3. Compaction is timed with the capacity that actually fits this Mac, not a
number that drifted.** This is the one that quietly costs you.
`dsh-compaction-basic` asks the provider for the route's capacity and compacts
at `thresholdRatio × capacity` (0.8 by default). The provider prefers the
server's **`max_model_len`** — Rapid-MLX's memory-fitted ceiling (what fits in
unified memory: weights + KV cache), in the vLLM/SGLang-standard field — over
the native `context_window`, and falls back to `context_window` on an older
server that doesn't report it. So compaction is timed to what the machine can
actually hold, not the model's advertised window (which it may not have room
for) and not a hand-written number copied from another model.

## Install

Needs Node ≥ 22.15 (dsh imports Node's Zstd stream API without declaring it)
and a running Rapid-MLX server.

```sh
# From npm:
dsh plugin --profile web add @raullenchai/dsh-provider

# …or straight from source — the package ships plain JS with no build step:
dsh plugin --profile web add github:raullenchai/rapid-mlx-dsh-provider

export RAPID_MLX_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000/v1     # optional; this is the default
dsh web
```

Then point the agent at the route:

```yaml
# $DSH_HOME/settings.yaml
agent-default-model:
  provider: rapid-mlx
  model: qwen3.6-35b-8bit
```

Verified: that command installs and activates as a profile layer against
`dsh 0.1.0-rc.7`. To hack on it locally instead, see
[Local development](#local-development).

## Model management (v0.2.0)

Beyond the provider route, the plugin registers five tools and a `/rapid-mlx`
command so the agent can see and manage models without leaving the session.
The split follows which surface actually owns each fact: served-model facts
come from the structured HTTP `/v1/models`; the download cache and pull/remove
are CLI-only, so those — and only those — shell out to `rapid-mlx` through the
harness subprocess seam.

| Tool | Source | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `rapid_mlx_serving` | HTTP `/v1/models` | The model(s) served right now, deduped, with context window, reasoning/tool parsers, MoE/hybrid, and modalities. |
| `rapid_mlx_cached` | `rapid-mlx models --cached` | Downloaded models and their on-disk size. |
| `rapid_mlx_pull` | `rapid-mlx pull <name>` | Download a model (alias or HF repo id). Cancellable; no fixed deadline. |
| `rapid_mlx_remove` | `rapid-mlx rm -y <name>` | Delete a cached model to free disk. |
| `rapid_mlx_health` | HTTP + `rapid-mlx --version` | API up? CLI reachable? Reported as two independent facts. |

`/rapid-mlx` prints a one-shot overview: health, the served model and its facts,
and total cache disk usage.

The CLI is resolved from the `cliCommand` config (default `rapid-mlx` on
`PATH`, or `$RAPID_MLX_CLI`); set it to an absolute path if the binary is not on
the harness's `PATH`. `rapid_mlx_pull`/`rapid_mlx_remove` are the only tools
that change anything on disk, and they run non-interactively (`rm` is forced
with `-y` because the subprocess seam ignores stdin).

## Verified

Against `dsh 0.1.0-rc.7` on an M3 Ultra:

- Installs and **activates as a profile layer** (no "declares no `dsh.bundle`"
  warning; the entry shows up in `dsh --profile headless --dump-config`).
- Registers the `rapid-mlx` route with `ctx.llm` and serves real queries.
- Plain chat, a single tool call, and the multi-step bug-fix task that gates
  Rapid-MLX releases — the last one fixed the bug and made the target repo's own
  test pass, verified independently, in 36 s on `qwen3.6-35b-8bit`.

## Not done yet

Being explicit, because the point of the adapter is to *use* what the server
says and some of it is still only read:

- `recommended_sampling` — should be applied automatically per model.
- `tool_call_parser` — should let `dsh` fail fast on a model that cannot emit
  `tool_calls`, instead of looping.
- `is_hybrid` / `is_moe` / `capabilities` — read, not yet acted on.
- **Memory-aware capacity.** Today `resolveModel()` reports the model's
  *advertised* context window. On a Mac the real ceiling is unified memory, and
  reporting that instead is the biggest remaining win — it needs Rapid-MLX to
  expose a usable-capacity figure first.
- Images are not carried through `stream()` — but they now **refuse** with
  `LlmError(..., 'UNSUPPORTED')` rather than being dropped, per the cookbook.
  Text, reasoning and tool calls are carried.
- The route is registered as `rapid-mlx`. If your `settings.yaml` also declares
  a `rapid-mlx` provider under `llm-pi-ai`, the two compete for one route name
  (`registerAdapter` owns provider exclusivity). Use one or rename ours.

## Conformance with the official adapter contract

Built against
[`docs/cookbook/adding-an-llm-adapter.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/main/docs/cookbook/adding-an-llm-adapter.md)
and its "protocol obligations" section. Each item has a test:

| Obligation | How it is met |
|---|---|
| `usage` before `finish`, nothing after `finish` | usage is buffered and flushed at end-of-stream, so a trailing usage-only chunk cannot reorder it |
| Tool-call `arguments` are raw JSON strings end to end | fragments stream as `argumentsDelta` and reassemble unparsed |
| Block indexes in first-seen order, reused per block | verified across a reasoning-then-text response |
| Errors take exactly two sanctioned paths | transport/protocol failures **throw** `LlmError` with a stable code; nothing ends the stream quietly |
| Honor `options.signal` | passed to `fetch` and to the SSE reader; an `AbortError` is re-thrown unchanged, not reclassified |
| A field the provider cannot honor throws `UNSUPPORTED` | image content refuses instead of being narrowed away |
| Config is a schemastery schema with env fallback | `export const Config`, fed from `cordis.patch.yml` via `!!js process.env.RAPID_MLX_BASE_URL` |

`finish.replayState` is not emitted: Rapid-MLX needs no native response ids
or signatures on follow-up calls, so there is nothing lossless to project.

## Three things worth knowing before you edit this

Each of these cost real

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-shutdown-idle

DSH 插件：**开启后，等所有会话都结束（没有任何 Agent 在跑）并保持空闲，自动执行关机**（也可选重启 / 休眠 / 睡眠 / 锁定 / 注销）。

## 用起来

1. 打开「设置 → 会话结束后关机」，点 **开启**。
2. 正常派活给任意会话；所有会话的回合结束后，插件先等 `空闲确认` 秒，再进入 `倒计时` 秒。
3. 倒计时结束即执行所选动作。期间任何会话重新开始运行，或点界面上的 **取消**，这次动作都会被撤销。

右上角（浮层右下角）在开启后会常驻一张小卡片，显示当前阶段与剩余秒数，并带「取消」按钮。**按住卡片标题即可拖动**：松手后位置写进浏览器 `localStorage`（键 `dsh.shutdown-idle.pill.position`），下次打开停在原处；拖动过程始终夹在视口内（留 8px 可见），窗口变小也会自动收回视野。从「取消」按钮上按下不会误触发拖动。

## 判据

- **会话进行中** = `ctx.get('agents').list()` 里存在 `status === 'running'` 的 Agent（与 dshmarket 的更新守卫同一判据）。这一条固定生效，不可关闭。
- **后台任务** = `ctx.get('jobs')` 中 `status === 'running'` 的作业（含各存活会话名下的作业），即 DSH 界面里的「后台任务」；由配置项 `considerJobs` 决定是否检测，关掉后完全不再统计。
- 拿不到 `agents` 服务时按 **不空闲** 处理：宁可不执行，也不误关机。
- 「必须观察到会话运行过」默认开启：刚开启且没有任何任务时不会执行动作。

## 参数

| 参数 | 默认 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 动作 | `shutdown` | `shutdown` / `restart` / `hibernate` / `sleep` / `lock` / `logoff` / `none`（`none` = 只记录不执行） |
| 空闲确认 | 20 秒 | 全部空闲后先确认这么久，避免回合间隙被误判为结束 |
| 倒计时 | 60 秒 | 可取消的执行前倒计时 |
| 必须观察到会话运行过 | 是 | 防止刚开启就执行 |
| 后台任务也算占用（`considerJobs`） | 是 | 关掉后完全不再检测后台任务（shell 作业） |

设置页把这几项收在「什么算『还在忙』」区块里：会话在跑固定算忙，下面两个复选框是配置项。

初始值来自本包 `cordis.patch.yml` 的行 `config`；界面改动写入 `<DSH_HOME>/dsh-shutdown-idle/settings.json` 并优先生效（删除该文件即回落到 patch 初始值）。

**开关状态不持久化**：宿主重启后一律是「关闭」，避免开机即误关机。

## 接口

| 方法 | 路径 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/dsh-shutdown/api/state` | 开关、阶段、倒计时、运行中会话/作业 |
| POST | `/dsh-shutdown/api/config` | `{ enabled?, action?, settleSeconds?, countdownSeconds?, requireActivity?, considerJobs? }` |
| POST | `/dsh-shutdown/api/cancel` | 取消倒计时并关闭开关 |
| GET | `/dsh-shutdown` | 客户端半不可用时的兜底页面 |

## 平台

动作命令是 Windows 自带的 `shutdown` / `rundll32`。非 Windows 平台上，除 `none` 外的动作会被降级为 `none` 并在界面标注，不会执行命令。

## 字段一览

- `host.v2.mjs` — Host 半：状态机、HTTP 接口、命令派发、兜底页面。（`host.v1.mjs` 为上一版，保留以便回滚。）
- `client.js` — 浏览器半：设置页分区 + `shell.overlay` 浮层卡片（可拖动，`useDraggable` 负责指针捕获、边界夹取与位置持久化）。
- `cordis.patch.yml` — bundle 补丁：插入插件行与初始配置。

升级宿主半代码时换文件名（`host.v1.mjs` → `host.v2.mjs`）并同步 `package.json` 的 `main` / `exports`：config-only 热重载不会重新加载同一路径的模块。

plugins.description: PCL 式 DSH 整合包：勾选已装第三方插件，导出小体积 .dshpack.zip 与一键安装命令串；导入先预览再按 spec 重新下载安装。Tiny modpack export/import for DeepSeek Harness plugins.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-modpack · DSH 整合包

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-modpack.svg?color=cb3837&logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-modpack)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/dsh-modpack.svg)](LICENSE)

> npm：<https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-modpack> · 仓库：<https://github.com/M1r0er/dsh-modpack> · MIT · DSH 插件（bundle）

像 Minecraft 的 PCL / HMCL 整合包那样管理 DSH 的第三方插件：

- **导出**：勾选本机已安装的第三方插件 → 生成一个只有清单和版本的小体积 `.dshpack.zip`（**不含插件代码、不含 `node_modules`**），同时给出一整串可直接复制执行的安装命令。
- **导入**：选择 `.dshpack.zip` 或直接粘贴命令串 → 先**预览**（已装同版本 / 版本不同 / 待安装 / 本地链接）→ 确认后再按 spec 重新下载安装；apply 前自动写 JSON 还原点。
- **发布**：把几十 KB 的 zip 发给别人，对方在「设置 → 整合包 → 导入」里预览后一键装齐。

导出的命令形如（示例，不会自动执行）：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-ops@0.3.0
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-better-sidebar@0.28.0
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:owner/repo#v1.0.0
```

## 为什么不是"备份插件"

DSH 已有若干备份/迁移工具（见 [docs/RELATED.md](docs/RELATED.md)），它们通常打包**配置、凭据或本地插件目录**，体积大、偏向"整机搬家"。
整合包的定位相反：**只记录"装哪些插件、哪个版本"**，插件本体在导入时从 npm / git 重新下载。这与 PCL 整合包"只有 mods 清单、不含游戏本体"是同一种取舍：

| | 备份 / 迁移工具 | dsh-modpack |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 包内容 | 配置文件、凭据、可能含本地插件源码 | 清单 + 版本 + 安装命令（可选脱敏配置） |
| 体积 | 几百 KB ~ 数 MB | 通常几 KB ~ 几十 KB |
| 适合 | 换电脑、回滚 | 发布、分享、复现一套插件组合 |
| 导入 | 覆盖配置 | 按 spec 重新下载插件，先预览再应用 |

同赛道还有一个更重的项目：[@dsh-packforge/dsh-pack-plugin](https://github.com/DSH-PackForge/dsh-pack-plugin)（`.dspack`）。它默认把 profile 配置与 `pnpm-lock.yaml` 一起打包，导入时用 pnpm 重建依赖，并绑定官方桌面端；其 README 自述 `export` / `install` 端到端仍需真实 pnpm 环境验证。dsh-modpack 选的是更轻的形态：只记录"装哪些插件、哪个版本"，并直接给出可复制的 `dsh plugin add` 命令串。完整对比见 [docs/RELATED.md](docs/RELATED.md)。

## 安装

在 DSH 里用插件管理器安装本目录（或发布后的 npm 包）：

```sh
dsh plugin add dsh-modpack
```

安装后：

- **设置 → 整合包**：图形界面，勾选 / 导出 / 导入；
- **模型工具**：`modpack_list`、`modpack_export`、`modpack_inspect`、`modpack_import`，也可以让 Agent 代劳。

> 本插件依赖 DSH 内置的 `pluginManager` 与 `configEditor` 服务。老版本 DSH 若没有 `pluginManager`，导出命令串仍可用，自动安装会报"服务不可用"。

## 图形界面

设置页分两块：

1. **导出**
   - 列出当前 profile 的第三方 bundle（含版本、是否本地链接）；
   - 默认全选可安装项，`link:` / 本地路径插件置灰并标注"不可分享"；
   - 可填名称 / 版本 / 作者 / 描述；
   - 可选"包含配置"：只收**选中插件**的 config override，疑似密钥默认替换为 `${REDACTED}`；
   - 导出后显示 zip 路径与命令块，可一键复制。
2. **导入**
   - 拖入 `.dshpack.zip`，或粘贴命令串；
   - 预览表逐条列出 `spec` 与状态 `installed-same / installed-different / missing / local / unknown`；
   - 点"应用安装"需二次确认；执行完显示每一步结果、还原点路径；需要重启的改动会单独提示。

## 命令行 / Agent 工具

```jsonc
// 列出可导出的插件
{ "tool": "modpack_list" }

// 导出（不写 zip，只拿命令串）
{ "tool": "modpack_export", "writeArchive": false, "include": ["dsh-ops", "dsh-context"] }

// 导出为 zip（默认写到 ~/.dsh/modpacks）
{ "tool": "modpack_export", "name": "我的整合包", "version": "1.0.0" }

// 导入预览（默认 apply=false，绝不安装）
{ "tool": "modpack_import", "path": "D:/packs/我的整合包-1.0.0.dshpack.zip" }

// 确认后应用
{ "tool": "modpack_import", "path": "…", "apply": true }
```

`modpack_import` 的安装动作走 `pluginManager.installBundle(spec, { saveExact: true })`，**不执行 shell，也不执行粘贴文本里的任何命令**——命令串只被解析成 spec。

## 整合包格式

`.dshpack.zip` 是一个普通 zip，内含：

| 文件 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `dshpack.json` | 清单：format/version、插件列表（name、version、spec、kind、bundle 行）、安装命令、可选 config |
| `install.ps1` / `install.sh` | 与清单一致的安装命令脚本 |
| `README.md` | 人类可读的说明 |

`dshpack.json` 关键字段见 [API.md](API.md)；`format` 固定为 `dsh-modpack`，`formatVersion` 为 1。导入时会校验格式版本，未来格式升级会给出明确提示。

## 安全

- 导出**从不安装**任何东西，也不联网。
- 导入默认只预览；`apply:true` 前会写 `<outDir>/backups/before-import-<时间>.json`。
- 包内不写插件代码；`config` 默认不导出，导出时会剔除密钥键与 `sk-` / `ghp_` / `xoxb-` 等明文 token。
- 本地链接插件（`link:` / 本地路径）不可移植：导出会标记并提示，导入时跳过，不会把别人的本地路径当成可下载 spec。
- 本插件的 HTTP 路由与 GUI 同源（`/modpack/*`），没有额外的跨域入口。

## 已知限制

- 只处理 **bundle**（`dsh.profile.bundles` / `package.json` 依赖）；随 DSH 发行的 installation 内置 bundle 不导出。
- 安装依赖目标机器能访问 npm / git，企业内网需要自行配置 registry。
- 版本对比是字符串精确比较；`name@latest` 这类浮动 spec 只能判断"已安装/未安装"。
- 不支持 zip64 / 加密 zip；整合包超过 32 MiB 会被拒绝（正常只有几 KB）。
- 配置导入（`withConfig` / 界面勾选）目前按 `patchId` 匹配本机行；行 id 被上游插件改名时会跳过并给出 reason。

## 开发

```sh
node --check index.js
node tests/zip.test.mjs
node tests/pack.test.mjs
node tests/host.test.mjs   # 用 mock Cordis 服务跑导出→预览→apply 全链路
```

- `lib/zip.mjs`：零依赖 zip 读写（store/deflate、CRC32、UTF-8 文件名）。
- `lib/pack.mjs`：清单构建/校验、spec 分类、命令解析、密钥剔除、diff。
- `index.js`：Host 半，接 `pluginManager` / `configEditor`，注册工具与 `/modpack/*` 路由。
- `client.js`：设置页，注册到 `settings.section`。

## 验证状态

- **2026-10-19 真机**（DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 / Windows）：重启后设置页已注册（`settings.section`，`id=modpack`，order 45，active）；`modpack_list` 读到 15 个第三方插件；`modpack_export` 生成 5.0 KiB 整合包 / 13 条安装命令（2 个本地链接自动跳过）；`modpack_inspect` 预览结果为 13 已装同版本 + 2 本地链接跳过。
- **离线**：18 项测试通过（zip 往返/CRC、命令解析、密钥剔除、mock Cordis 全链路、client 模块注册），详见 [docs/VERIFICATION.md](docs/VERIFICATION.md)。

## License

MIT

plugins.description: 记住 DeepSeek Harness 桌面版的窗口尺寸：重启后自动恢复、默认水平垂直居中，并提供设置页手动调整。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-window-size

**简体中文** · [English](README.en.md)

记住 **DeepSeek Harness 桌面版**的窗口尺寸：重启后自动恢复、默认水平垂直居中，并且可以在设置页里直接改，不用手动拖窗口。

![平台：Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows-0078D4)
![宿主：DSH 桌面版](https://img.shields.io/badge/host-DSH%20Desktop-4f6ef7)
![许可证：MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)

- **首次启动**：没有记录时使用 **1440 × 900**，并居中。
- **每次手动调整**：自动记录，下次启动恢复。
- **默认居中**：每次启动都把窗口放在当前显示器工作区正中；可在设置页关闭，改为沿用上次位置。
- **不会记错**：最大化、最小化、隐藏状态一律不记录，避免下次以超大尺寸打开；恢复时会按当前显示器工作区收缩，换显示器也能用。
- **设置页**：`设置 → 窗口尺寸` 可手动设定尺寸、记住当前尺寸、立即居中、恢复默认。
- 在非桌面版 Host（`dsh` 命令行、服务器）上仍可加载，但设置页会提示不可用。

## 为什么必须做成 Host 插件

桌面版创建主窗口时把尺寸写死为 `1280 × 820`，也不持久化任何窗口状态。渲染端改不了它：在 Electron 里，`window.resizeTo()` 会被路由到 `WebContentsDelegate::SetContentsBounds`，Electron 只把它转发成 `content-bounds-updated` 事件，**并不会真的改变 `BrowserWindow` 的大小**。

所以真正干活的是 Host 进程：它通过 `koffi`（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop-host` 本来就依赖它）调用 `FindWindowExW` / `GetWindowRect` / `GetDpiForWindow` / `SetWindowPos`，并且**抢在窗口显示前**完成设置，避免先闪一下旧尺寸。

## 设置页

`设置 → 窗口尺寸` 是一个 `settings.section` 条目。页面上会显示当前窗口尺寸、已记录尺寸和上次动作（含时间），并提供：

| 控件 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| 宽度 / 高度 + **应用并记住** | 立刻改变窗口尺寸并保存 |
| **记住当前尺寸** | 把你现在手动拖出来的尺寸存下来 |
| **重新应用** | 用记录值再应用一次（含当前居中设置） |
| **恢复默认** | 回到配置的默认 `1440 × 900` |
| **启动时居中** 开关 | 决定恢复时是否居中 |
| **立即居中** | 只居中，不改尺寸 |
| **启用尺寸记忆** 开关 | 关闭后既不恢复也不记录 |

页面本身不碰窗口，它通过包私有 RPC 通道 `/dsh-window-size` 调用 Host 端，Host 端用与启动恢复同一个控制器来执行。

## 安装

直接从 GitHub 安装（插件管理器里填写）：

```
github:home-i/dsh-window-size#v1.1.1
```

也可以在桌面版 **插件** 页里从本地目录安装。本地开发还可以把包链接进桌面版 profile：

```jsonc
// ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "dsh-window-size": "link:/path/to/dsh-window-size"
  },
  "dsh": {
    "profile": {
      "bundles": ["...", "dsh-window-size"]
    }
  }
}
```

下次启动即生效，之后改动源码也不需要重装。

> 不要把这个 `link:` 换成手工建的 Windows junction 再执行 `pnpm install`：pnpm 安装时会移除该条目，而 Windows 会顺着 junction 进入目标目录，导致源码目录被清空。

## 配置

Loader 行里配置首次启动的默认值：

```yaml
# cordis.patch.yml
- insert:
    - id: dsh-window-size
      name: dsh-window-size
      config:
        width: 1440        # 首次启动宽度，CSS 像素
        height: 900        # 首次启动高度，CSS 像素
        center: true       # 每次恢复都居中
        enabled: true      # 是否启用恢复与记录
```

尺寸单位是 CSS 像素；宽高最小被限制为 `520 × 600`，恢复时还会被当前显示器工作区限制。

## 状态文件

记录放在 harness home 下，跟随 profile 而不是 Electron 的 `userData`：

```
~/.dsh/dsh-window-size/window-size.json
```

```json
{
  "size": { "width": 1440, "height": 900 },
  "center": true,
  "enabled": true,
  "last": { "action": "restore", "source": "remembered", "at": 0 },
  "updatedAt": 0
}
```

`last` 记录最近一次动作（`restore`、`resize`、`apply`、`remember`、`center`、`center-on`、`center-off`、`enabled`、`disabled`），包含实际达成的尺寸、DPI 缩放和窗口标题——设置页显示的就是它，出问题时也靠它定位。删除这个文件即回到配置默认值。旧版（只有 size + last）的记录会自动升级：尺寸保留，新开关取配置默认。

## RPC 约定

Host 在 Web carrier 上注册前缀路由，每个请求都先过 `connection.admit`，因此只有本 Host 的已认证页面能操作窗口：

```
POST /dsh-window-size/<endpoint>
content-type: application/json

{ "type": "client-request", "rpcId": "…", "method": "<endpoint>", "payload": … }
```

端点：`status`、`apply`（`{width,height}`）、`reapply`、`reset`、`center`、`remember`、`set-center`（`true|false`）、`set-enabled`（`true|false`）。返回使用 Connection 的 `server-response` 信封；业务失败以 HTTP 200 + `{ ok: false, error: { code, message, details } }` 返回，而路由不存在、非 POST、认证失败分别是 `404` / `405` / `401`。

## 文件

| 文件 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Host 插件入口；启动控制器与 RPC，并负责释放 |
| `window-memory.js` | 控制器：查找窗口、恢复、居中、跟踪缩放、处理页面动作 |
| `rpc.js` | 前缀路由注册、认证、信封解析、端点分发 |
| `win32.js` | koffi 绑定、DPI、显示器工作区、窗口查找 |
| `state.js` | harness home 下的原子 JSON 记录 |
| `client.js` | 设置页（`settings.section`），中英双语 |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | bundle 层插入的 Loader 行 |

## 环境要求

- Windows 10/11 x64 或 arm64。
- DeepSeek Harness **桌面版**（Electron shell 的 Host 进程）。窗口 API 是 Win32 的，其它环境不生效。

## 常见问题

**包管理器操作时报 `dsh: cannot resolve profile bundle "dsh-window-size"`**：说明 manifest 里列了这个 bundle，但 `node_modules/dsh-window-size` 不存在、或其链接目标里没有 `package.json`。插件管理器的 reconcile 阶段对所有已列依赖都会严格解析、没有兜底（而启动时只是跳过并报告），补回链接或重装 bundle 即可恢复。

**设置页显示不可用**：当前 Host 不是桌面版，或 `koffi` / `user32` 加载失败；具体原因会显示在提示下方。

**窗口恢复后的尺寸不对**：查看状态文件里的 `last`，它记录了请求值、实际达成值、DPI 缩放与窗口标题。

[MIT](LICENSE) © home-i
